title: Turkey switches to a Latin alphabet
summary: A law of 1 November 1928 replaced the Arabic-based Ottoman script, used for Turkish for over 1,000 years, with a Latin alphabet, at Ataturk's personal initiative.
why: A nation changed its script by law; literacy rose sharply afterward, helped by many other reforms.

notes.problem: 'Exact figures are disputed' is not in the source; source says literacy rose from about 10% to over 90% but other factors also contributed.
